options: A protocol that requires a persistent connection between client and server
An architectural style for designing APIs around resources, not a product or protocol
A file format Oracle Fusion stores data in
A programming language
questions.explain: REST is a set of design conventions, described by Roy Fielding, not a protocol or product.

questions.q: In Oracle Fusion's REST API, what does a "resource" refer to?
options: A noun-like 'thing' — an invoice, journal, or customer — each addressed by its own URL
The server's CPU allocation
A type of HTTP status code
The username used to log in
questions.explain: Resources are the nouns REST organizes an API around, like invoices or journals.

questions.q: Why does every call to Oracle Fusion's REST API need to include credentials, even right after a previous call?
options: Because Oracle Fusion is always offline
Because the REST server is stateless and remembers nothing about previous calls
Because credentials expire every millisecond
This isn't true — Fusion remembers your login like the web UI does
questions.explain: Statelessness means each request is self-contained; nothing is remembered server-side between calls.

questions.q: Which URL follows REST's resource-based convention for an Oracle Fusion invoice with ID 300000182?
options: POST /getInvoiceById?id=300000182
GET /fscmRestApi/resources/11.13.18.05/invoices/300000182
GET /runInvoiceLookup
POST /invoiceAction?type=get
questions.explain: This addresses the invoice resource directly by its URL, letting the GET verb express the action.

questions.q: Instead of custom action names, what does REST reuse to express what happens to a resource?
options: Custom query parameters only
A separate action-description file uploaded with every request
The standard HTTP methods — GET, POST, PATCH, DELETE
The resource's internal database table name
questions.explain: REST reuses HTTP's existing verbs instead of inventing action-specific endpoint names.
